title: 第17集
transcript: The grown-ups, to be sure, will not believe you when you tell them that. They imagine that they fill a great deal of space. They fancy themselves as important as the baobabs. You should advise them, then, to make their own calculations. They adore figures, and that will please them. But do not waste your time on this extra task. It is unnecessary. You have, I know, confidence in me.

When one wishes to play the wit, he sometimes wanders a little from the truth. I have not been altogether honest in what I have told you about the lamplighters. And I realize that I run the risk of giving a false idea of our planet to those who do not k now it. Men occupy a very small place upon the Earth. If the two billion inhabitants who people its surface were all to stand upright and somewhat crowded together, as they do for some big public assembly, they could easily be put into one public square twenty miles long and twenty miles wide. All humanity could be piled up on a small Pacific islet.
"Ah! Then there are no people on the Earth?"
"Good evening," said the snake.
"This is the Earth; this is Africa," the snake answered.
"What planet is this on which I have come down?" asked the little prince.

When the little prince arrived on the Earth, he was very much surprised not to see any people. He was beginning to be afraid he had come to the wrong planet, when a coil of gold, the color of the moonlight, flashed across the sand.
"Good evening," said the little prince courteously.
The little prince sat down on a stone, and raised his eyes toward the sky.
"I wonder," he said, "whether the stars are set alight in heaven so that one day each one of us may find his own again… Look at my planet. It is right there above us. But how far away it is!"
"This is the desert. There are no people in the desert. The Earth is large," said the snake.
"It is beautiful," the snake said. "What has brought you here?"
"I have been having some trouble with a flower," said the little prince.
The little prince made no reply.
The little prince smiled.
"I solve them all," said the snake.
"But I am more powerful than the finger of a king," said the snake.
And they were both silent.
"Whomever I touch, I send back to the earth from whence he came," the snake spoke again. "But you are innocent and true, and you come from a star…"
The little prince gazed at him for a long time.
"Oh! I understand you very well," said the little prince. "But why do you always speak in riddles?"
"It is also lonely among men," the snake said.
He twined himself around the little prince's ankle, like a golden bracelet.
"You are not very powerful. You haven't even any feet. You cannot even travel…"
And they were both silent.
"You move me to pity -- you are so weak on this Earth made of granite," the snake said. "I can help you, some day, if you grow too homesick for your own planet. I can --"
"I can carry you farther than any ship could take you," said the snake.
"Where are the men?" the little prince at last took up the conversation again. "It is a little lonely in the desert…"
"You are a funny animal," he said at last. "You are no thicker than a finger…"
"Ah!" said the snake.
translation: 大人们当然不会相信你的话。他们想象自己占了很大的空间。他们自以为像猴面包树一样重要。你应该劝他们自己去计算。他们酷爱数字，那会让他们高兴。但别把时间浪费在这额外的任务上。这是不必要的。我知道，你对我有信心。
一个人想要卖弄聪明时，有时会稍微偏离真相。关于点灯人，我对你讲的并不完全诚实。我意识到，我冒着向那些不了解我们星球的人提供错误印象的风险。人类在地球上占的地方非常小。如果居住在地球表面的二十亿人口都站立起来并稍微挤在一起，就像在大型公众集会时那样，他们可以轻松地被放进一个边长二十英里的广场里。全人类可以堆放在太平洋的一个小岛上。
“啊！那么地球上没有人吗？”
“晚上好，”蛇说。
“这是地球；这是非洲，”蛇回答道。
“我降落的这是什么行星？”小王子问。
小王子到达地球时，非常惊讶竟看不到任何人。他开始害怕自己来错了行星，这时，一道金色的光，月光的颜色，划过沙地。
“晚上好，”小王子有礼貌地说。
小王子坐在一块石头上，抬眼望向天空。
“我想知道，”他说，“星星是否在天上被点亮，以便有一天我们每个人都能重新找到自己的星星？看我的星球。它就在我们上方。但它是多么遥远啊！”
“这是沙漠。沙漠里没有人。地球很大，”蛇说。
“真美，”蛇说。“是什么把你带到这里来的？”
“我为一朵花而烦恼，”小王子说。
小王子没有回答。
小王子笑了。
“我把它们全都解决了，”蛇说。
“但我的力量比国王的手指还大，”蛇说。
他们俩都沉默了。
“无论我触碰谁，我都会把他送回他来时的大地，”蛇又说。“但你是无辜而真诚的，你来自一颗星星……”
小王子长时间地凝视着他。
“哦！我非常理解你，”小王子说。“但你为什么总是说话像谜语？”
“在人群之中也同样孤独，”蛇说。
他像金手镯一样缠绕在小王子的脚踝上。
“你并不强大。你甚至没有脚。你甚至无法旅行……”
他们俩都沉默了。
“你让我怜悯——你在这由花岗岩构成的地球上如此弱小，”蛇说。“如果你太过思念自己的星球，总有一天我可以帮助你。我可以——”
“我能把你带到任何船都到不了的远方，”蛇说。
“人在哪里？”小王子终于重新开口。“在沙漠里有点孤独……”
“你是个有趣的动物，”他最后说。“你比手指还细……”
“啊！”蛇说。
